_comment: EXAMPLE · Salesforce SOQL source. SalesforceSrc.queries is a list that today takes EXACTLY ONE entry, so 'several objects' means several publishers: read_accounts and read_opportunities are one per object, independently triggered and independently failing — and, unlike a multi-query SQL source, they do NOT share a consistent snapshot, so join defensively downstream. There is no SELECT * in SOQL, which is why every query lists its fields. `$lastModified` in the SOQL is substituted with initial_last_modified (a query using the token with no cutoff is rejected before it runs) but the cutoff DOES NOT ADVANCE between runs — unlike a file source, which advances it for you, or a SQL source, where ctx does. So it is a static FLOOR (read_recent_accounts), and read_new_opportunities shows the two-layer incremental pattern that follows: a cheap floor in the SOQL plus a ctx-held watermark filtering the batch to what is new (ISO-8601 sorts lexicographically, so a string compare is a time compare). read_with_deleted covers include_deleted — queryAll, the only way a mirror learns about deletions, since an ordinary read just stops returning the row — plus api_version and src_cfg (logging_level is a NUMERIC level; the string "INFO" fails inside the plugin at run time). DESTRUCTIVE SETUP: create-data on a salesforce domain WIPES every Account and Opportunity in the org before bulk-loading the model — point it at a scratch org. One function per file under functions/salesforce_soql/. Run: `tdx-xp oneshot --suite examples/salesforce_soql`.
